source.text: בַּשְּׁבִיעִ֕י בְּעֶשְׂרִ֥ים וְאֶחָ֖ד לַחֹ֑דֶשׁ הָיָה֙ דְּבַר־יְהוָ֔ה בְּיַד־חַגַּ֥י הַנָּבִ֖יא לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: In the seventh, on [the] twenty-first of the month, the word of Yahweh came by [the] hand of Haggai the prophet, saying:

en.L: In the seventh [month], on the twenty-first [day] of the month, the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came by the hand of Haggai the prophet, saying:
en.B: In the seventh month, on the twenty-first day of the month, the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came through the prophet Haggai:
en.R: On the twenty-first day of the seventh month of the year, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave this message through the prophet Haggai:

decisions.choice: the seventh month, the twenty-first day: mid-October 520 BC, the last day of the Festival of Booths
decisions.reason: The date is about 17 October 520 BC, less than a month after the work began (1:15). The Festival of Booths ran from the fifteenth to the twenty-first of the seventh month (Leviticus 23:34-36, 39-43). At that festival Solomon had dedicated the first temple (1 Kings 8:2), so the comparison in verse 3 with the house in its former glory would be on everyone's mind. The harvest being celebrated was a poor one (1:10-11). |

decisions.choice: no year is given: it is the year of 1:15
decisions.reason: The verse gives the month and the day but not the year. The second year of Darius, at the end of 1:15, is meant; some read those words as the beginning of this verse (see the note at 1:15). |

decisions.choice: the Hebrew form of the date at every level
decisions.reason: The date keeps its Hebrew form, as set for Haggai. Literal brackets "month" and "day", which the Hebrew leaves out. Readable says "the seventh month of the year". |

source.text: אֱמָר־נָ֗א אֶל־זְרֻבָּבֶ֤ל בֶּן־שַׁלְתִּיאֵל֙ פַּחַ֣ת יְהוּדָ֔ה וְאֶל־יְהוֹשֻׁ֥עַ בֶּן־יְהוֹצָדָ֖ק הַכֹּהֵ֣ן הַגָּד֑וֹל וְאֶל־שְׁאֵרִ֥ית הָעָ֖ם לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: Speak, please, to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and to the remnant of the people, saying:

en.L: Speak now to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and to Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and to the people's remnant, saying:
en.B: Speak to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and to the rest of the people, and say:
en.R: Speak to Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, and to all the people who are left. Ask them:

decisions.choice: speak now: a command with a softening word
decisions.reason: The Hebrew adds a small word to the command, often rendered "please" or "now". It does not make the command less firm. |

decisions.choice: the remnant of the people: the community that had returned from exile
decisions.reason: As in 1:12, the remnant is the people who had come back to Judah. |

decisions.choice: Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, governor of Judah, and Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest
decisions.reason: The names keep the wording of 1:1 at each level. |

source.text: מִ֤י בָכֶם֙ הַנִּשְׁאָ֔ר אֲשֶׁ֤ר רָאָה֙ אֶת־הַבַּ֣יִת הַזֶּ֔ה בִּכְבוֹד֖וֹ הָרִאשׁ֑וֹן וּמָ֨ה אַתֶּ֜ם רֹאִ֤ים אֹתוֹ֙ עַ֔תָּה הֲל֥וֹא כָמֹ֛הוּ כְּאַ֖יִן בְּעֵינֵיכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Who among you [is] the one left who saw this house in its former glory? And how do you see it now? Is it not like it, as nothing in your eyes?

en.L: Who among you is left who saw this house in its first glory? And how do you see it now? Is it not as nothing in your eyes?
en.B: Who among you is still here who saw this house in its former glory? And how do you see it now? Does it not look like nothing at all to you?
en.R: Who among you is old enough to have seen this temple in its former glory? What does it look like to you now? Does it not seem like nothing at all?

decisions.choice: who saw this house in its former glory: the oldest people, who remembered Solomon's temple
decisions.reason: The first temple was destroyed in 587 BC, sixty-seven years before. A few of the oldest people could remember it. When the foundation of the new temple was laid, those old men wept aloud, while the younger ones shouted for joy (Ezra 3:12). |

decisions.choice: glory: splendor, honor, weight
decisions.reason: The word means weight, and so honor and splendor. It is used of the beauty of Solomon's temple, and also of the LORD's own presence that filled it (1 Kings 8:11). Haggai uses it of both in verses 7 and 9. |

decisions.choice: as nothing in your eyes: of no account
decisions.reason: Compared with the old temple, the new building looks like nothing at all. The Hebrew says literally "is it not like it, as nothing", that is, "is not such a house as nothing". |

decisions.choice: glory at every level
decisions.reason: "Glory" follows the Isaiah table for this word at every level, here and in verses 7 and 9. Readable says "temple" for "house", as in chapter 1. |

source.text: וְעַתָּ֣ה חֲזַ֣ק זְרֻבָּבֶ֣ל׀נְאֻם־יְהוָ֡ה וַחֲזַ֣ק יְהוֹשֻׁ֣עַ בֶּן־יְהוֹצָדָק֩ הַכֹּהֵ֨ן הַגָּד֜וֹל וַחֲזַ֨ק כָּל־עַ֥ם הָאָ֛רֶץ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֖ה וַֽעֲשׂ֑וּ כִּֽי־אֲנִ֣י אִתְּכֶ֔ם נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And now, be strong, Zerubbabel, declaration of Yahweh; and be strong, Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest; and be strong, all [the] people of the land, declaration of Yahweh, and work; for I [am] with you, declaration of Yahweh of hosts.

en.L: But now be strong, Zerubbabel, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}; and be strong, Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest; and be strong, all the people of the land, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and work; for I am with you, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts.
en.B: Now be strong, Zerubbabel, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Be strong, Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest. And be strong, all the people of the land, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and get to work, for I am with you, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.
en.R: But now, Zerubbabel, be strong, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest, be strong. Everyone who lives in the land, be strong, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Get to work, because I am with you, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

decisions.choice: be strong ... for I am with you: the words spoken to Joshua son of Nun and to Solomon
decisions.reason: The LORD told Joshua son of Nun, as he took up Moses' work, "Be strong ... for the LORD your God is with you" (Joshua 1:6-9). David told Solomon the same as he gave him the plans for the first temple (1 Chronicles 22:13-16; 28:20). Now a later Joshua, with the heir of David's line, hears the same words for the building of the second temple. |

decisions.choice: all the people of the land: the whole community living in Judah
decisions.reason: Here the phrase means all the people, alongside their leaders (compare 2 Kings 11:14). In Ezra 4:4 a similar phrase is used of the neighbors who opposed the building, but that is not the sense here. |

decisions.choice: work: get to work, act
decisions.reason: The verb means "do, act". After the call to be strong, it means to take up the work on the temple. |

decisions.choice: Joshua son of Jehozadak, the high priest; and work (L), get to work (B, R)
decisions.reason: The name keeps the wording of 1:1. Readable puts each name before its call, so that each leader is addressed in turn. |

source.text: אֶֽת־הַדָּבָ֞ר אֲשֶׁר־כָּרַ֤תִּי אִתְּכֶם֙ בְּצֵאתְכֶ֣ם מִמִּצְרַ֔יִם וְרוּחִ֖י עֹמֶ֣דֶת בְּתוֹכְכֶ֑ם אַל־תִּירָֽאוּ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: [With] the word that I cut with you when you came out of Egypt, and my Spirit standing in your midst. Do not fear.

en.L: [Remember] the word that I made with you when you came out of Egypt, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Spirit is standing in your midst; do not fear.
en.B: This is the promise I made with you when you came out of Egypt, and {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} Spirit still stands among you. Do not be afraid.
en.R: Remember what I promised you when you came out of Egypt. My Spirit is still with you. Do not be afraid.

decisions.choice: the word that I made with you: a sentence with no main verb
alternatives: as the word I made with you
keep the word I made with you
decisions.reason: The verse begins with the sign of a direct object, but no verb comes before it. It may be read with "I am with you" in verse 4 ("according to the word I made with you"), or with a verb understood, such as "remember" or "this is". The Greek translation is generally said to lack the first half of the verse. The sense is plain: the LORD's covenant promise from the exodus still holds.

decisions.choice: made: literally "cut", the verb used for making a covenant
decisions.reason: A covenant was "cut" (Genesis 15:10, 18), because animals were cut in two when it was sealed. The word here is the promise of that covenant: "I will be your God, and you will be my people" (Exodus 6:7; Leviticus 26:12). |

decisions.choice: my Spirit standing in your midst: the LORD's Spirit present with his people
decisions.reason: When Israel came out of Egypt, the LORD put his Spirit among them and led them (Isaiah 63:11-14; Numbers 11:17, 25; Nehemiah 9:20). The same Spirit is with the builders. Zechariah, preaching at the same time, says the temple will be built "not by might, nor by power, but by my Spirit" (Zechariah 4:6). |

decisions.choice: [Remember] (L), This is (B), Remember (R); Spirit with a capital S
decisions.reason: Each level supplies a verb so that the sentence can be read (m1); Literal brackets it. God's Spirit is written with a capital S, as in Isaiah.

source.text: כִּ֣י כֹ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת ע֥וֹד אַחַ֖ת מְעַ֣ט הִ֑יא וַאֲנִ֗י מַרְעִישׁ֙ אֶת־הַשָּׁמַ֣יִם וְאֶת־הָאָ֔רֶץ וְאֶת־הַיָּ֖ם וְאֶת־הֶחָרָבָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: For thus says Yahweh of hosts: Yet once, it [is] a little [while], and I [am] shaking the heavens and the earth and the sea and the dry land.

en.L: For thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: Yet once more, in a little while, I am shaking the heavens and the earth and the sea and the dry ground.
en.B: For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: Once more, and soon, I will shake heaven and earth, sea and dry land.
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: Soon I will shake the sky and the earth, the sea and the land, one more time.

decisions.choice: once more I will shake the heavens and the earth: quoted in Hebrews 12:26
decisions.reason: Hebrews 12:26-27 quotes this verse in the wording of the Greek translation ("Yet once more I will shake not only the earth but also heaven"). The writer compares the shaking of the earth at Sinai (Exodus 19:18) with a final shaking, and reads "once more" as meaning that what can be shaken will be removed, so that the unshakable kingdom remains. The verse here is translated from the Hebrew. |

decisions.choice: once more, in a little while: soon, and one more time
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is compressed: "yet one, it is a little". "Once more" recalls the earlier shaking of the earth when God came down at Sinai (Exodus 19:18; Judges 5:4-5). "A little while" says that it will be soon.

decisions.choice: shake the heavens and the earth: the LORD's coming to overturn the powers of the world
decisions.reason: The shaking of all creation is the sign of the LORD coming to act (Joel 4:16; Isaiah 13:13). Verse 7 and verses 21-22 show what it means: the nations and their kingdoms are shaken. |

decisions.choice: once more (L, B), one more time (R)
decisions.reason: Every level keeps "once more", which Hebrews takes up (m1). |

source.text: וְהִרְעַשְׁתִּי֙ אֶת־כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֔ם וּבָ֖אוּ חֶמְדַּ֣ת כָּל־הַגּוֹיִ֑ם וּמִלֵּאתִ֞י אֶת־הַבַּ֤יִת הַזֶּה֙ כָּב֔וֹד אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will shake all the nations, and [the] treasure of all the nations will come, and I will fill this house [with] glory, says Yahweh of hosts.

en.L: And I will shake all the nations, and the treasures of all the nations will come, and I will fill this house full of glory, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts.
en.B: I will shake all the nations, and the wealth of all the nations will come in. I will fill this house with glory, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.
en.R: I will shake all the nations, and their riches will be brought here. I will fill this temple with glory, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

decisions.choice: the treasures of all the nations: the valuable things of the nations
decisions.reason: The word means "what is desired, precious". Its verb is plural ("they will come"), so it is usually read as the treasures of the nations, which verse 8 explains: the silver and gold are the LORD's. Isaiah 60:5-11 also pictures the wealth of the nations brought to Zion. The Latin translation reads "the desired one of all nations will come", and from it came the traditional reading "the desire of all nations", taken by many Christians as a title of the Messiah. The Hebrew wording favors the treasures.

decisions.choice: glory: splendor, and the LORD's own presence
decisions.reason: The house will be filled with splendor from the treasures, and also with the LORD's glory, as his glory filled the tabernacle and Solomon's temple (Exodus 40:34-35; 1 Kings 8:10-11). |

decisions.choice: treasures (L), wealth (B), riches (R)
decisions.reason: The levels follow m1. Readable says "will be brought here" for "will come", since treasures do not walk. |

source.text: לִ֥י הַכֶּ֖סֶף וְלִ֣י הַזָּהָ֑ב נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: Mine [is] the silver, and mine [is] the gold, declaration of Yahweh of hosts.

en.L: Mine [is] the silver, and {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}} [is] the gold, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts.
en.B: The silver belongs to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and the gold belongs to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.
en.R: All the silver and gold belong to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

decisions.choice: the silver and the gold are mine: all wealth belongs to the LORD
decisions.reason: The builders are poor, and the new house looks like nothing beside the old (verse 3). But all the world's wealth is the LORD's (Psalm 24:1; 50:10-12; 1 Chronicles 29:14-16), and he can bring it to his house when he chooses. |

decisions.choice: Mine ... mine (L, B), belong to me (R)
decisions.reason: The pronoun takes the deity_pronoun setting except where it begins the sentence. |

source.text: גָּד֣וֹל יִֽהְיֶ֡ה כְּבוֹד֩ הַבַּ֨יִת הַזֶּ֤ה הָאַֽחֲרוֹן֙ מִן־הָ֣רִאשׁ֔וֹן אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת וּבַמָּק֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ אֶתֵּ֣ן שָׁל֔וֹם נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃פ

records.literal_gloss: Great will be the glory of this house, the latter, more than the former, says Yahweh of hosts; and in this place I will give peace, declaration of Yahweh of hosts.

en.L: Greater will be the latter glory of this house than the first, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts; and in this place I will give peace, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts.
en.B: The glory of this house in the future will be greater than its glory in the past, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies. And in this place I will give peace, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.
en.R: This temple will be more glorious than it was before, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies. And in this place I will give peace, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

decisions.choice: the latter glory of this house: the glory the house will have, greater than the glory it had
alternatives: the glory of this latter house will be greater than that of the former
decisions.reason: The word "latter" can go with "glory" or with "house". Haggai treats the temple as one house, which the old people saw "in its former glory" (verse 3), so the reading here is "the latter glory of this house". The other reading compares the new house with the first one. The promise is the same.

decisions.choice: peace: well-being, safety and wholeness
decisions.reason: The word means far more than the absence of war: it is wholeness, security and well-being (Isaiah 9:6; Jeremiah 29:7). It comes from the LORD, in the place where his house stands. |

decisions.choice: a promise beyond what Haggai's hearers saw
decisions.reason: The temple finished in 515 BC never matched Solomon's in splendor, and the ark was gone. The promises of verses 6-9 point beyond the building of Haggai's day to the time when the LORD would come to his house (Malachi 3:1). |

decisions.choice: peace at every level
decisions.reason: "Peace" follows the Isaiah table. "Glory" stays at every level; Readable says "more glorious". |

source.text: בְּעֶשְׂרִ֤ים וְאַרְבָּעָה֙ לַתְּשִׁיעִ֔י בִּשְׁנַ֥ת שְׁתַּ֖יִם לְדָרְיָ֑וֶשׁ הָיָה֙ דְּבַר־יְהוָ֔ה אֶל־חַגַּ֥י הַנָּבִ֖יא לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: On [the] twenty-fourth of the ninth, in [the] second year of Darius, the word of Yahweh came to Haggai the prophet, saying:

en.L: On the twenty-fourth of the ninth, in the second year of Darius, the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Haggai the prophet, saying:
en.B: On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, in Darius's second year, the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to the prophet Haggai:
en.R: On the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month of the year, in Darius's second year as king, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave this message to the prophet Haggai:

decisions.choice: the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month: mid-December 520 BC
decisions.reason: The date is about 18 December 520 BC, three months after the work began (1:15). The ninth month (Kislev) came after the early rains, when the winter grain was sown. |

decisions.choice: came to Haggai: a message given to the prophet himself
decisions.reason: This time the word comes "to" Haggai, not "by the hand of" him to others: he is to put questions to the priests (verses 11-13) and then give the people the answer. |

decisions.choice: the Hebrew form of the date at every level
decisions.reason: The date keeps its Hebrew form, as in 1:1. Literal leaves out "day" and "month", as the Hebrew does (compare 1:15). Readable says "as king", which is understood. |

source.text: כֹּ֥ה אָמַ֖ר יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֑וֹת שְׁאַל־נָ֧א אֶת־הַכֹּהֲנִ֛ים תּוֹרָ֖ה לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: Thus says Yahweh of hosts: Ask, please, the priests [for] instruction, saying:

en.L: Thus says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts: Ask now the priests for instruction, saying:
en.B: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says this: Ask the priests for instruction on this question:
en.R: This is what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies says: Ask the priests to give a ruling from the law:

decisions.choice: instruction: a priest's ruling on a question of the law
decisions.reason: The word (torah) means teaching or instruction. The priests were to teach the people the difference between holy and common, clean and unclean (Leviticus 10:10-11), and to give rulings on hard cases (Deuteronomy 17:8-11; Malachi 2:7). Haggai asks them for such a ruling. |

decisions.choice: instruction (L, B), a ruling from the law (R)
decisions.reason: Literal and Balanced keep "instruction", as the Isaiah table sets. Readable says "a ruling from the law", because here the word means a priest's answer to a particular question (m1). |

source.text: הֵ֣ן׀יִשָּׂא־אִ֨ישׁ בְּשַׂר־קֹ֜דֶשׁ בִּכְנַ֣ף בִּגְד֗וֹ וְנָגַ֣ע בִּ֠כְנָפוֹ אֶל־הַלֶּ֨חֶם וְאֶל־הַנָּזִ֜יד וְאֶל־הַיַּ֧יִן וְאֶל־שֶׁ֛מֶן וְאֶל־כָּל־מַאֲכָ֖ל הֲיִקְדָּ֑שׁ וַיַּעֲנ֧וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֛ים וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ לֹֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: If a man carries holy flesh in [the] fold of his garment, and touches with his fold the bread or the cooked food or the wine or oil or any food, will it become holy? And the priests answered and said, No.

en.L: "If someone carries holy meat in the fold of {{gender:their|his}} garment, and with the fold touches bread or stew or wine or oil or any food, will it become holy?" And the priests answered and said, "No."
en.B: "Suppose someone carries consecrated meat in the fold of {{gender:their|his}} garment, and the fold touches bread or stew, wine or oil, or any other food. Does that food become holy?" The priests answered, "No."
en.R: "Suppose someone is carrying meat from a sacrifice in a fold of their clothes, and the clothes touch some bread, stew, wine, olive oil, or any other food. Will that food become holy?" The priests answered, "No."

decisions.choice: holy meat in the fold of a garment: meat from a sacrifice, carried in a fold of the robe
decisions.reason: Meat from many sacrifices was holy and was to be eaten in a holy place (Leviticus 6:19-20 in the Hebrew numbering, 6:26-27 in many other Bibles; Jeremiah 11:15). A fold of a long robe served as a pocket. The law says that whatever touches the holy flesh becomes holy (Leviticus 6:20); the question is whether holiness passes on further, from the garment to a third thing. |

decisions.choice: the priests answered, No: holiness does not pass on at second hand
decisions.reason: The priests rule that the food is not made holy, because only the garment touched the meat. Verse 13 asks the matching question about uncleanness. |

decisions.choice: someone ... their garment (gender default)
decisions.reason: The word for "man" here means anyone, so the gender setting is used; Readable says "their clothes", which is already inclusive. The questions and answers are in double quotes, as prose quotes speech. |

source.text: וַיֹּ֣אמֶר חַגַּ֔י אִם־יִגַּ֧ע טְמֵא־נֶ֛פֶשׁ בְּכָל־אֵ֖לֶּה הֲיִטְמָ֑א וַיַּעֲנ֧וּ הַכֹּהֲנִ֛ים וַיֹּאמְר֖וּ יִטְמָֽא׃

records.literal_gloss: And Haggai said, If one unclean by a dead body touches any of these, will it become unclean? And the priests answered and said, It will become unclean.

en.L: And Haggai said, "If one who is unclean from a dead body touches any of these, will it become unclean?" And the priests answered and said, "It will become unclean."
en.B: Then Haggai asked, "If someone who is unclean from contact with a dead body touches any of these, does it become unclean?" The priests answered, "Yes, it becomes unclean."
en.R: Then Haggai asked, "Suppose someone has become unclean by touching a dead body. If that person touches any of these foods, will the food become unclean?" The priests answered, "Yes, it will."

decisions.choice: unclean from a dead body: the strongest kind of uncleanness
decisions.reason: Touching a dead body made a person unclean for seven days, and whatever that person touched became unclean too (Numbers 19:11-22). |

decisions.choice: uncleanness spreads where holiness does not
decisions.reason: Together, the two answers make Haggai's point: holiness does not pass on easily, but uncleanness does. Being near the holy place does not make a person holy, but an unclean person defiles what he touches. |

decisions.choice: Yes, it becomes unclean (B); Yes, it will (R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew answers by repeating the verb, which is how Hebrew says "yes". |

source.text: וַיַּ֨עַן חַגַּ֜י וַיֹּ֗אמֶר כֵּ֣ן הָֽעָם־הַ֠זֶּה וְכֵן־הַגּ֨וֹי הַזֶּ֤ה לְפָנַי֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וְכֵ֖ן כָּל־מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה יְדֵיהֶ֑ם וַאֲשֶׁ֥ר יַקְרִ֛יבוּ שָׁ֖ם טָמֵ֥א הֽוּא׃

records.literal_gloss: And Haggai answered and said, So [is] this people and so [is] this nation before me, declaration of Yahweh, and so [is] all [the] work of their hands; and what they offer there [is] unclean.

en.L: And Haggai answered and said, "Such is this people, and such is this nation before {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and such is all the work of their hands; and what they offer there is unclean."
en.B: Then Haggai said, "So it is with this people and this nation in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sight, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and so it is with everything they do; whatever they offer there is unclean."
en.R: Then Haggai said, "This is what these people are like in {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} sight, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. Everything they do is unclean, and so is every offering they bring to the altar."

decisions.choice: so is this people: unclean, and their offerings with them
decisions.reason: Haggai applies the rulings to the people. The text does not say what made them unclean. In the setting of the book it is most likely their neglect of the LORD's house (1:4, 9), during which their offerings on the altar could not make them holy, while their own state made their offerings unclean. Some think of contact with the mixed peoples of the land, but the book does not mention it.

decisions.choice: what they offer there: the sacrifices on the altar
decisions.reason: The altar had been rebuilt when the exiles first returned, and sacrifices were offered there even while the temple lay in ruins (Ezra 3:2-6). |

decisions.choice: the Greek translation adds lines at the end of the verse
decisions.reason: The Greek translation is generally said to add several lines here, about gain gained unjustly and about hating the one who reproves in the gate, words that recall Amos 5:10. They are not in the Hebrew text and are not translated.

decisions.choice: this people ... this nation
decisions.reason: The LORD says "this people" and "this nation", not "my people", as in 1:2. Readable says "bring to the altar" for "offer there" (m2). |

source.text: וְעַתָּה֙ שִֽׂימוּ־נָ֣א לְבַבְכֶ֔ם מִן־הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה וָמָ֑עְלָה מִטֶּ֧רֶם שֽׂוּם־אֶ֛בֶן אֶל־אֶ֖בֶן בְּהֵיכַ֥ל יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: And now, set, please, your heart from this day and upward: before [the] placing of a stone on a stone in [the] temple of Yahweh,

en.L: And now, set your heart, please, from this day and upward: before stone was laid on stone in the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}},
en.B: So now, think carefully about how things have been up to this day, before one stone was laid on another in {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple:
en.R: Now think carefully about what life was like before you started to rebuild {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple.

decisions.choice: from this day and upward: back from this day
decisions.reason: The phrase can look forward ("from this day on") or back. Here what follows looks back to the time before the building began (verses 15-17), and verse 18 repeats the phrase looking forward to the blessing (verse 19). Some read it as forward in both places.

decisions.choice: before stone was laid on stone: before the work on the temple began
decisions.reason: Laying one stone on another is the start of building. The time before is the time of neglect described in 1:6-11. |

decisions.choice: think carefully (B, R), set your heart (L)
decisions.reason: "Set your heart" follows 1:5 at each level. Balanced and Readable make plain that the look is backward (m1). Readable says "before you started to rebuild" for "before stone was laid on stone".

source.text: מִֽהְיוֹתָ֥ם בָּא֙ אֶל־עֲרֵמַ֣ת עֶשְׂרִ֔ים וְהָיְתָ֖ה עֲשָׂרָ֑ה בָּ֣א אֶל־הַיֶּ֗קֶב לַחְשֹׂף֙ חֲמִשִּׁ֣ים פּוּרָ֔ה וְהָיְתָ֖ה עֶשְׂרִֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: since they were, one came to a heap of twenty, and it was ten; one came to the wine vat to draw fifty [from the] press, and it was twenty.

en.L: since those days, one came to a heap of twenty [measures], and there were ten; one came to the wine vat to draw fifty [measures from] the press, and there were twenty.
en.B: how, when someone came to a heap of grain expecting twenty measures, there were only ten, and when someone came to the wine vat to draw fifty measures, there were only twenty.
en.R: In those days, when someone went to a pile of grain expecting twenty measures, there were only ten. When someone went to the wine vat expecting to draw fifty measures of wine, there were only twenty.

decisions.choice: since those days: through that whole time
decisions.reason: The first word is hard. It may mean "since they were", that is, through all that time. Some suggest a small change to read "how did you fare?". The sense of the verse is plain either way.

decisions.choice: the heap and the wine vat: grain on the threshing floor, wine in the vat below the press
decisions.reason: Threshed grain was piled in a heap on the threshing floor and measured out. Grapes were trodden in a press, and the juice ran into a vat cut in the rock below, from which it was drawn off. The harvests gave half, or less than half, of what was expected. |

decisions.choice: a heap of grain expecting twenty measures (B); only ten (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew names only the numbers. Balanced and Readable add "grain", "measures" and "expecting" to make the comparison plain. No unit is named, so none is given. |

source.text: הִכֵּ֨יתִי אֶתְכֶ֜ם בַּשִּׁדָּפ֤וֹן וּבַיֵּֽרָקוֹן֙ וּבַבָּרָ֔ד אֵ֖ת כָּל־מַעֲשֵׂ֣ה יְדֵיכֶ֑ם וְאֵין־אֶתְכֶ֥ם אֵלַ֖י נְאֻם־יְהוָֽה׃

records.literal_gloss: I struck you with blight and with mildew and with hail, all [the] work of your hands; and not you to me, declaration of Yahweh.

en.L: I struck you with blight and with mildew and with hail, all the work of your hands; yet you [did] not [return] to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.B: I struck you, and all the work of your hands, with blight and mildew and hail, yet you did not return to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.
en.R: I struck your crops with diseases that dried them out and turned them yellow, and I sent hail on all your work. But even then you did not come back to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: blight and mildew ... yet you did not return to me: the words of Amos 4:9
decisions.reason: Amos 4:9 has "I struck you with blight and with mildew ... yet you did not return to me, declares the LORD". The plagues are among the curses of the covenant (Deuteronomy 28:22; 1 Kings 8:37). Haggai applies the old words to his own day. |

decisions.choice: not you to me: you did not turn to me
decisions.reason: The Hebrew is very short, "and not you to me", with no verb. The words of Amos 4:9 show the sense: "you did not return to me". The Greek translation is generally said to read "you did not return to me" here too.

decisions.choice: blight and mildew: crop diseases
decisions.reason: The first word means scorching, as by the hot east wind; the second a yellowing of the grain, a kind of mildew or rust. Hail beat down crops and vines (Exodus 9:25). |

decisions.choice: the wording of Amos 4:9 at each level
decisions.reason: Where Haggai uses the words of Amos 4:9, each level uses the wording published there: "blight and with mildew ... yet you did not return to me" (L, B) and "diseases that dried them out and turned them yellow ... But even then you did not come back to me" (R). Literal brackets the words the Hebrew leaves out. |

source.text: שִׂימוּ־נָ֣א לְבַבְכֶ֔ם מִן־הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה וָמָ֑עְלָה מִיּוֹם֩ עֶשְׂרִ֨ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֜ה לַתְּשִׁיעִ֗י לְמִן־הַיּ֛וֹם אֲשֶׁר־יֻסַּ֥ד הֵֽיכַל־יְהוָ֖ה שִׂ֥ימוּ לְבַבְכֶֽם׃

records.literal_gloss: Set, please, your heart from this day and upward, from [the] twenty-fourth day of the ninth, from the day that [the] temple of Yahweh was founded; set your heart:

en.L: Set your heart, please, from this day and onward, from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth [month], from the day that the temple of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was founded; set your heart:
en.B: Think carefully from this day on, from the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month, from the day the foundation of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple was laid. Think carefully:
en.R: Think carefully about what will happen from today on. Today is the twenty-fourth day of the ninth month. Today the foundation of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}'s temple has been laid. Think about it.

decisions.choice: the day that the temple of the LORD was founded: this very day
alternatives: the day of the first foundation in 536 BC
decisions.reason: The foundation of the second temple was first laid soon after the exiles returned (Ezra 3:10). Here "the day that the temple was founded" is this day, the twenty-fourth of the ninth month, so the words probably refer to a ceremony of laying the foundation anew, or to the formal restart of the work.

decisions.choice: from this day and onward: now looking forward
decisions.reason: In verse 15 the phrase looked back. Here it looks ahead: from this day the LORD will bless (verse 19).

decisions.choice: set your heart (L), think carefully (B, R)
decisions.reason: The call keeps the wording of 1:5 at each level. |

source.text: הַע֤וֹד הַזֶּ֨רַע֙ בַּמְּגוּרָ֔ה וְעַד־הַגֶּ֨פֶן וְהַתְּאֵנָ֧ה וְהָרִמּ֛וֹן וְעֵ֥ץ הַזַּ֖יִת לֹ֣א נָשָׂ֑א מִן־הַיּ֥וֹם הַזֶּ֖ה אֲבָרֵֽךְ׃ס

records.literal_gloss: [Is] the seed still in the granary? And even the vine and the fig tree and the pomegranate and the olive tree have not borne. From this day I will bless.

en.L: Is the seed still in the storehouse? And even the vine and the fig and the pomegranate and the olive tree have not borne [fruit]. From this day I will bless [you].
en.B: Is there still any seed left in the barn? Even the vine, the fig tree, the pomegranate and the olive tree have not yet borne fruit. But from this day on I will bless you.
en.R: Is any seed left in the barn? The grapevines, fig trees, pomegranate trees and olive trees have not produced any fruit yet. But from today on I will bless you.

decisions.choice: the seed, the vine, the fig, the pomegranate, the olive: the harvests still to come
decisions.reason: By the ninth month the winter seed had been sown, so none was left in the storehouse, and the fruit trees would not bear until the summer. Nothing could yet be seen of the coming harvest. The LORD promises the blessing before there is any sign of it. |

decisions.choice: I will bless: I will give you good harvests
decisions.reason: The verb has no object in the Hebrew; the people and their harvests are meant (compare Deuteronomy 28:8). |

decisions.choice: [fruit], [you] (L); fruit, you (B, R)
decisions.reason: The Hebrew leaves out what the trees bear and whom the LORD will bless. |

source.text: וַיְהִ֨י דְבַר־יְהוָ֤ה׀שֵׁנִית֙ אֶל־חַגַּ֔י בְּעֶשְׂרִ֧ים וְאַרְבָּעָ֛ה לַחֹ֖דֶשׁ לֵאמֹֽר׃

records.literal_gloss: And the word of Yahweh came a second time to Haggai on [the] twenty-fourth of the month, saying:

en.L: And the word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came a second time to Haggai on the twenty-fourth [day] of the month, saying:
en.B: The word of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} came to Haggai a second time on the twenty-fourth day of the month:
en.R: On that same day, the twenty-fourth day of the month, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} gave Haggai a second message:

decisions.choice: a second time, on the twenty-fourth: the same day as verse 10
decisions.reason: Haggai's last two messages came on the same day, about 18 December 520 BC. |

decisions.choice: On that same day (R)
decisions.reason: Readable says plainly that it is the day of verse 10. |

source.text: אֱמֹ֕ר אֶל־זְרֻבָּבֶ֥ל פַּֽחַת־יְהוּדָ֖ה לֵאמֹ֑ר אֲנִ֣י מַרְעִ֔ישׁ אֶת־הַשָּׁמַ֖יִם וְאֶת־הָאָֽרֶץ׃

records.literal_gloss: Say to Zerubbabel, governor of Judah, saying: I [am] shaking the heavens and the earth.

en.L: Speak to Zerubbabel, governor of Judah, saying: I am shaking the heavens and the earth.
en.B: Tell Zerubbabel, governor of Judah: I am going to shake the heavens and the earth.
en.R: Tell Zerubbabel, governor of Judah: I am going to shake the sky and the earth.

decisions.choice: I am shaking the heavens and the earth: the words of verse 6, now spoken to Zerubbabel
decisions.reason: The promise of verse 6 is repeated to the governor alone. What the shaking means for him follows in verses 22-23. |

decisions.choice: Zerubbabel, governor of Judah
decisions.reason: The name and title keep the wording of 1:1, without "son of Shealtiel", which the Hebrew does not have here. |

source.text: וְהָֽפַכְתִּי֙ כִּסֵּ֣א מַמְלָכ֔וֹת וְהִ֨שְׁמַדְתִּ֔י חֹ֖זֶק מַמְלְכ֣וֹת הַגּוֹיִ֑ם וְהָפַכְתִּ֤י מֶרְכָּבָה֙ וְרֹ֣כְבֶ֔יהָ וְיָרְד֤וּ סוּסִים֙ וְרֹ֣כְבֵיהֶ֔ם אִ֖ישׁ בְּחֶ֥רֶב אָחִֽיו׃

records.literal_gloss: And I will overthrow [the] throne of kingdoms and destroy [the] strength of [the] kingdoms of the nations, and I will overthrow chariotry and its riders; and horses and their riders will go down, each by [the] sword of his brother.

en.L: And I will overturn the throne of kingdoms, and I will destroy the might of the kingdoms of the nations; and I will overturn the chariot and its riders, and horses and their riders will go down, each by the sword of his brother.
en.B: I will overturn the thrones of kingdoms and shatter the power of the nations' kingdoms. I will overturn chariots and their drivers; horses and riders will go down, each by the sword of his comrade.
en.R: I will overthrow kings and destroy the power of the nations. I will turn over chariots and their drivers. Horses and their riders will fall, and the soldiers will kill one another with their swords.

decisions.choice: overthrow ... horses and their riders: the overthrow of Sodom and of Pharaoh's army
decisions.reason: The verb "overthrow" is the one used for the destruction of Sodom and Gomorrah (Genesis 19:25). Horse and rider recall the song at the Red Sea: "horse and its rider he has thrown into the sea" (Exodus 15:1). The LORD will act against the world's powers as he did then. |

decisions.choice: each by the sword of his brother: the enemy soldiers kill one another
decisions.reason: In panic the enemy turns on itself, as the Midianites did before Gideon (Judges 7:22; 1 Samuel 14:20; Ezekiel 38:21). |

decisions.choice: the throne of kingdoms: royal power
decisions.reason: "Throne" stands for the rule of kings. The kingdoms are not named; the Persian empire was the great power of Haggai's day. |

decisions.choice: thrones (B), kings (R); his comrade (B), one another (R)
decisions.reason: "Brother" here means a fellow soldier; Balanced says "comrade" and Readable "one another". The soldiers are men, so no gender setting is used. |

source.text: בַּיּ֣וֹם הַה֣וּא נְאֻם־יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֡וֹת אֶ֠קָּחֲךָ זְרֻבָּבֶ֨ל בֶּן־שְׁאַלְתִּיאֵ֤ל עַבְדִּי֙ נְאֻם־יְהוָ֔ה וְשַׂמְתִּ֖יךָ כַּֽחוֹתָ֑ם כִּֽי־בְךָ֣ בָחַ֔רְתִּי נְאֻ֖ם יְהוָ֥ה צְבָאֽוֹת׃

records.literal_gloss: In that day, declaration of Yahweh of hosts, I will take you, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, my servant, declaration of Yahweh, and I will set you like a signet ring, for I have chosen you, declaration of Yahweh of hosts.

en.L: In that day, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts, I will take you, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and I will set you like a signet ring; for you I have chosen, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of hosts.
en.B: On that day, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, I will take you, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}, and make you like a signet ring, for I have chosen you, declares {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.
en.R: At that time, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies, I will take you, Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} servant, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. I will make you like the ring with {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} seal on it, because I have chosen you, says {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} of Armies.

decisions.choice: like a signet ring: the reversal of Jeremiah 22:24
decisions.reason: The LORD had said of King Jehoiachin (Coniah), Zerubbabel's grandfather, "even if you were the signet ring on my right hand, I would pull you off" (Jeremiah 22:24). Now he takes Jehoiachin's grandson and makes him his signet ring. The rejection of David's line is not the LORD's last word. |

decisions.choice: signet ring: the seal that carries its owner's authority
decisions.reason: A signet ring was used to stamp a seal on documents and goods, and stood for its owner's authority (Genesis 41:42; Esther 8:8). It was kept close and guarded (Song of Songs 8:6). |

decisions.choice: my servant ... I have chosen you: titles of David's line
decisions.reason: "My servant" and "chosen" are words used of David and the king of his line (2 Samuel 3:18; Psalm 78:70; 89:4, 21). The promise looks to the future of David's house. Zerubbabel never became king, and the hope passed to a later son of David; Matthew 1:12-13 and Luke 3:27 name Zerubbabel among the ancestors of Jesus. |

decisions.choice: my servant at every level; a signet ring (L, B), the ring with my seal on it (R)
decisions.reason: "Servant" is kept at every level for this title, as for "my servant" in Isaiah. Readable explains the signet ring as Jeremiah 22:24 does at Readable. Zerubbabel takes no deity_pronoun span. |
